short_name: White House National AI Policy Framework (2026)
full_name: National Policy Framework for the Responsible Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
summary: Non-binding policy framework developed under EO 14179 directing federal agencies toward AI adoption and innovation. Sets voluntary principles for responsible AI use in federal government but creates no private sector obligations.
notable: Guidance only — no binding effect on private sector. Successor document to various Biden-era OSTP guidance documents.

summary: Voluntary framework providing practical guidance to private sector organisations deploying AI. Addresses internal governance, operations management, and human-AI interaction. Updated in 2020. No enforcement mechanism.
notable: Widely referenced as 'soft law' model; Singapore explicitly chose voluntary approach over mandatory AI regulation.

full_name: AI Verify — AI Governance Testing Framework and Toolkit
summary: Voluntary AI testing framework and toolkit allowing companies to validate responsible AI claims against international principles. Not binding; participation is voluntary. Used by companies for voluntary compliance attestation.

full_name: Guidelines for AI Developers — Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry
issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
summary: Non-binding guidance for AI developers covering transparency, safety, fairness, accountability, and security. Japan's primary AI governance instrument prior to the 2025 AI Promotion Act. Based on Hiroshima AI Process principles agreed by G7.
notable: Pre-dates binding AI Promotion Act (2025). Voluntary; enforcement through sector-specific laws only.

full_name: Voluntary AI Safety Standard for Australian Businesses
issuing_body: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
summary: Australia's voluntary standard providing ten guardrails for responsible AI use in high-risk settings. Published September 2024 as interim measure while government considered whether to mandate guardrails. Government confirmed in December 2025 it will NOT make these mandatory.
notable: Government rejected mandatory guardrails December 2025 — this remains voluntary guidance only.

full_name: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA) — Part of Bill C-27 (terminated)
issuing_body: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
summary: Canada's proposed AI regulation establishing risk-based obligations for high-impact AI systems. Bundled with PIPEDA privacy modernization. TERMINATED when Parliament was prorogued January 5, 2025. Canada currently has no federal AI law.
notable: TERMINATED. Parliament prorogued January 2025; all bills died. Canada remains without federal AI legislation as of April 2026.

full_name: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: Voluntary framework for managing AI risks throughout the AI lifecycle. Structured around four functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. Widely adopted by US companies and referenced in state AI laws. Not binding but operationally influential.
notable: Mandated as a baseline for federal agency AI adoption under EO 14110 (since revoked). Voluntary for private sector.
